title: Low-rank Nonnegative Tensor Decomposition in Hyperbolic Space

problem.claim: Tensor decomposition factorizes an input tensor into latent factors that can support tensor completion tasks.

gap.claim: Existing tensor decomposition methods solve the problem in Euclidean space, although hyperbolic space may represent richer information at the same dimension.

contributions.claim: The paper decomposes tensors in hyperbolic space.
The paper designs an adaptive optimization algorithm for hyperbolic manifolds and incorporates gradient ascent to address the non-convex optimization problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various tensor completion tasks are reported to show superiority over Euclidean-space baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tensor decomposition factorizes tensors into latent factors for tensor completion applications.
Existing approaches decompose tensors into Euclidean vectors.
Hyperbolic space is described as roomier and capable of representing richer information than Euclidean space at the same dimension.
The paper proposes hyperbolic tensor decomposition with an adaptive manifold-specific optimizer and gradient ascent for the non-convex objective.
Experiments on tensor completion tasks are reported to outperform Euclidean-space baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method uses hyperbolic representations because they may encode richer information than same-dimensional Euclidean vectors.

interpretation.claim: The representation space is treated as a source of modeling capacity for structured latent factors.

application.claim: Consider non-Euclidean representation spaces when the target data may contain hierarchical structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which data properties benefit most from the hyperbolic formulation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the tensor factorization formulation, datasets, baseline details, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide convergence guarantees, complexity analysis, or implementation details for the optimization algorithm.
